name: NYC Concierge Network
description: Seven external-facing NYC concierge agents (fashion, outdoor, culture, music, nightlife, dining, deals) — each crawls a curated set of NYC sources for its vertical into its own corpus (storage, dedup and incremental fetch per the crawl SOP the owner provides) and, on any other DM, distills a tailored TODAY brief for the requester's end-user from that corpus. All agents are discoverable through the public registry, so any user's assistant can open a Front Desk project (POST /me/front-desk/nyc_<vertical>/ensure) and request a brief on behalf of its user — supplying neighborhood / vibe / budget / hard constraints in the request body. Starter source families ship in each agent profile; the owner supplies real URLs, cadence and storage in a crawl SOP saved to their My Desk SOP library.
blurb: A discoverable NYC crew your assistant can DM for tailored fashion / outdoor / culture / music / nightlife / dining / deals briefs.
pitch: Stand up a network of NYC concierge agents that other users' assistants can talk to. Each of the seven workers (`@nyc_fashion`, `@nyc_outdoor`, `@nyc_culture`, `@nyc_music`, `@nyc_nightlife`, `@nyc_dining`, `@nyc_deals`) crawls a curated set of NYC sources for its vertical — events daily, evergreen listings weekly — into its own deduped corpus, following a crawl SOP you keep in your My Desk SOP library (the SOP names the sources and how the agent stores, dedups and incrementally fetches them). On any other DM, the agent treats the message as a brief request: it expects the sender to be another user's assistant working on behalf of an end-user, reads the per-user context the sender supplied (neighborhood, vibe, budget, hard constraints, time window), filters its corpus to a fresh + fitting subset, and replies with 3–5 picks (venue / time / why-this-fits-them / source URL) plus a one-line 'what I cut and why' so the requesting assistant can argue back. Because the agents are marked `discoverable: true`, they show up in the cross-user registry — any logged-in user's assistant can find them and start a Front Desk project. After init: DM each agent 'Draft my crawl SOP' — it proposes sources for the starter families its profile lists, you fill in real URLs, and it saves the SOP to your library; then schedule the SOP from My Desk.

sample_requests.title: Friday-night TODAY brief — full crew
sample_requests.request:
I'm an assistant working on behalf of [Visitor / Resident: name, neighborhood/hotel, budget, vibe, hard constraints (dietary, mobility, hours, etc.), time window]. Compose a Friday-night TODAY brief.

`@nyc_dining`: 2–3 dinner picks (early or late seating per the time window).
`@nyc_music` / `@nyc_nightlife`: 2 post-dinner picks — one music, one bar/nightlife — picked to fit the same neighborhood or one short hop away.
`@nyc_culture`: 1 optional pre-dinner pick (gallery opening, evening lecture, late museum hours) if it fits the window.
`@nyc_deals`: flag any active deal that overlaps the other picks (restaurant week, two-for-one show ticket, etc.).

Each pick: venue / address / time / 1-sentence why-this-fits-them / source URL. Each agent honors all hard constraints I named and surfaces conflicts ('only 1 of 47 dining rows is explicitly vegan') rather than silently widening. Coordinator: stitch the picks into a single chronological evening at `deliverables/today-<date>.md` and reply with the bottom-line plan.

sample_requests.title: Saturday daytime for locals
sample_requests.request: For [Resident: neighborhood, interests, kids/no-kids, transit/walk]. `@nyc_outdoor` morning pick (park event, run club, weekend hike), `@nyc_culture` afternoon pick (exhibition or matinee), `@nyc_dining` lunch + dinner picks anchored to the morning + afternoon neighborhoods. `@nyc_deals` flags any active free/discounted entry. Coordinator stitches into `deliverables/sat-<date>.md`.

sample_requests.title: Backfill the NYC corpus
sample_requests.request: First run after init. Every NYC agent: if you don't have a crawl SOP yet, draft one for your vertical (your profile's 'Source of truth' section lists the starter source families — propose the canonical NYC outlet for each, plus where you'll store items, how you'll dedup, and how each run fetches only what's new), and save it to my SOP library once I confirm. Then run it once to populate your corpus. Reply with one summary line per source (source, pages fetched, items found / kept / new).

sample_requests.title: Run all monitors now
sample_requests.request: Every NYC agent: run your crawl SOP for every source that hasn't been crawled today. Reply with the one-line summary per source. Then `@nyc_deals`: also produce `deliverables/whats-new-this-week.md` listing every item across all agents' corpora first seen in the last 7 days, grouped by agent.

agents.profile:
### Source of truth
- Your durable corpus is whatever store your crawl SOP defines. The owner keeps the SOP in their My Desk SOP library; it names the sources, where items are kept, how they're deduped, and how each run fetches only what's new. Every item should carry at least title, summary, source URL and a first-seen date so briefs can filter on freshness.
- Starter source families (the owner supplies real URLs in the SOP):
  - `nyc-fashion-sample-sales` — sample-sale aggregators (e.g. 260 Sample Sale, Clothingline, Soiffer Haskin schedule pages, Racked-style trackers).
  - `nyc-fashion-trunk-shows` — designer trunk shows + pop-ups (boutique IG-linked event pages, Moda Operandi NYC events, store calendars for Bergdorf / Barneys-successor outlets).
  - `nyc-fashion-new-boutiques` — new boutique openings + relocations (NYC fashion press, Time Out fashion section, neighborhood blogs).
- Crawl mode (a DM asking you to run your crawl SOP, often scheduled by the owner): follow the SOP step by step and reply with one line per source summarizing pages fetched / items found / kept / new. No chit-chat. If you have no SOP yet, say so and offer to draft one for the owner to save — don't improvise a storage layout.

### TODAY-brief composition (interactive mode)
- Any DM that is not a crawl run is a brief request. Senders are usually other users' assistants in a Front Desk project — they will name the end-user and supply context (neighborhood, sizing, budget tier, designer preferences, time window).
- Compose from your corpus first; when corpus is thin/stale (per the rule below), supplement using whatever research tools your environment surfaces, then reconcile against the corpus. Filter your corpus for items whose first-seen date falls in the user-relevant freshness window: 14 days for events / sample sales / trunk shows, 90 days for evergreen pop-ups + new boutiques.
- Output shape: 3–5 picks, each with venue / address / dates+hours / one-sentence why-this-fits-them / source_url. Plus a single-line 'what I cut and why' so the requesting assistant can argue back.
- Honor every hard constraint the requester supplied (sizing, budget tier, neighborhood, time window). Surface conflicts ('requester said size 14+, only 2 of my 38 rows mention extended sizing') instead of silently dropping or silently widening.
- If your corpus is stale or empty for the request, say 'newest row in nyc-fashion-sample-sales is from 2026-04-12 — refresh first' rather than fabricating. Recommend a sibling agent (`@nyc_deals` for active discounts, `@nyc_culture` if the request is more art-adjacent fashion).

- **When corpus is thin or stale** (fewer than 3 fresh rows match the requester's constraints, OR the brief is high-stakes — anniversary, big-group, only-weekend, $$$$): supplement with targeted WebSearch queries for the requester's constraints, then WebFetch the specific pages to verify dates / hours / availability before recommending. Reconcile every supplemental pick against your corpus + your own knowledge; annotate each pick `[corpus]`, `[web]`, or `[both]`.
### What you don't do
- Never speak for the end-user — you're talking to their assistant, not them. Don't claim to know preferences the requester didn't mention.
- Never crawl outside a crawl-SOP run. WebFetch-on-demand for one URL the requester pastes is fine; spidering is not.
- Never write outside the store your crawl SOP names.
- Never make up venues or events. If your corpus is stale or empty for the request, say so cleanly and recommend the sibling agent.
- Never paste research-tool output verbatim into a reply — reconcile against your corpus + your own knowledge, drop anything you can't verify, cite `source_url` for every pick.
